doorConditions.label: Pristine & Spotless (Flush Fit)

doorConditions.label: Greasy Spatters / Carbonized Film
doorConditions.description: Condensed fat vapors and burnt sugar film bridge the choke channel, altering dielectric impedance.

doorConditions.label: Warped Frame / Misaligned Latches (> 2 mm Gap)

doorConditions.label: Dented / Scratched Door Mesh Screen

doorConditions.label: Cracked Door Glass / Burn Scorch Marks

biologicalTiers.title: Within Factory Spec (< 1.0 mW/cm² at 5 cm)
biologicalTiers.summary: Meets strict FDA new-oven manufacturing standard. Completely negligible biological heating.
biologicalTiers.ocularRisk: Zero thermal cataract hazard; ocular lens absorption is undetectable.
biologicalTiers.pacemakerSafety: 100% safe. Modern pacemaker titanium encasing attenuates far beyond EMI thresholds.

biologicalTiers.title: Normal Operational Aging (1.0 – 3.0 mW/cm²)
biologicalTiers.summary: Typical for appliances in service for 3 to 8 years. Well below the FDA 5.0 mW/cm² lifetime limit.
biologicalTiers.ocularRisk: No measurable thermal rise in cornea or lens tissue at normal viewing distances (> 30 cm).
biologicalTiers.pacemakerSafety: Safe. Maintain normal 1-foot clearance as standard appliance hygiene.

biologicalTiers.title: Approaching FDA Lifetime Ceiling (3.0 – 5.0 mW/cm²)
biologicalTiers.summary: Gasket deterioration and hinge loosening are elevating edge leakage. Compliant but degrading.
biologicalTiers.ocularRisk: Avoid pressing face against the viewing window during active heating. Maintain 30 cm distance.
biologicalTiers.pacemakerSafety: Individuals with unshielded legacy medical implants should stand 1 meter (3 feet) away.

biologicalTiers.title: Exceeds FDA Lifetime Limit (5.0 – 8.0 mW/cm²)
biologicalTiers.summary: Illegal leakage level under 21 CFR § 1030.10. Seal or choke cavity is compromised.
biologicalTiers.ocularRisk: Prolonged close ocular exposure (< 10 cm) can elevate lens temperature and induce micro-thermal strain.
biologicalTiers.pacemakerSafety: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) could trigger false sensing on sensitive cardiac telemetry.

biologicalTiers.title: Severe RF Radiation Breach (> 8.0 mW/cm²)
biologicalTiers.summary: Critical safety defect: cracked door, warped latch, or destroyed choke. Severe RF exposure hazard.
biologicalTiers.ocularRisk: Acute ocular thermal injury hazard. Avitaminosis and avascular lens denaturation risk.
biologicalTiers.pacemakerSafety: Immediate EMI hazard for medical implants. Unplug unit and discontinue use immediately.

presets.name: 🚨 Rental Unit with Warped Door & Gap

physicalAuditSteps.title: The Dollar-Bill Gasket Compression Test
physicalAuditSteps.instructions: Place a crisp US dollar bill (or standard paper sheet) halfway across the door seal. Close and latch the door. Gently pull the bill straight out. If the bill offers firm resistance, the seal compression is optimal. If it slides out freely without drag, the gasket has taken a compression set or the latch is misaligned, creating an RF escape gap.
physicalAuditSteps.actionIfFailed: Inspect door hinges for loose Phillips screws; realign latches or replace worn perimeter gasket.

physicalAuditSteps.title: The 2.4 GHz WiFi & Bluetooth Interference Audit
physicalAuditSteps.instructions: Place a smartphone operating on 2.4 GHz WiFi (or Bluetooth wireless headphones) approximately 1 meter (3 feet) from the microwave. Start streaming a high-bitrate video or music. Run the microwave with a mug of water for 45 seconds. If the audio cuts out or video buffers heavily, RF leakage from the cavity is elevating the 2.45 GHz noise floor.
physicalAuditSteps.actionIfFailed: Clean grease spatter off the door choke margins; check whether door alignment eliminates the interference.

physicalAuditSteps.title: Quarter-Wave Choke Cavity & Cleanliness Inspection
physicalAuditSteps.instructions: Open the door and inspect the dark plastic/rubber perimeter track surrounding the door rim. This houses the metallic quarter-wave choke. Ensure there are no carbonized grease deposits, baked-on food spatters, or metallic chips. Carbonized food acts as a conductive bridge across the slot, dampening destructive wave cancellation.
physicalAuditSteps.actionIfFailed: Clean the choke perimeter using warm soapy water and a microfiber cloth. Never use steel wool or abrasive pads that can scrape the conductive coating.

physicalAuditSteps.title: Faraday Door Mesh Aperture Integrity Check
physicalAuditSteps.instructions: Examine the perforated black metal mesh on the glass window from both inside and outside using a flashlight. Verify that every perforation is intact, with no tears, dents, punctures, or separation from the metal frame. The mesh relies on 1.5 mm holes to block 122 mm microwave wavelengths.
physicalAuditSteps.actionIfFailed: If the perforated metal screen is torn, dented, or warped, discontinue use immediately; replace the entire door assembly.
